model_result.answer_summary: The fatty acid in PL1 is RCOOH = C18H32O2 (linoleic acid; PL1 is tetralinoleoyl cardiolipin, C81H142O17P2 in its non-ionised form). Derivation: the a-d fragment assembly with the 5.1 value n = 1 gives PL1 atom inventory C = 9 + 4cR, H = 13 + n + 8cR - 8u, O = 17, P = 2 (consistent with the page-4 hydrolysis PL1 + 8H2O -> 4RCOOH + 2H3PO4 + 3 glycerol); the handshake (valence) count gives total sigma+pi bonds = (93 + n + 24cR - 8u)/2 = 255 with n = 1, i.e. 3cR - u = 52; reductive ozonolysis to three different equimolar products forces u + 1 = 3, so u = 2 and cR = 18. Consistency with the 5.4 data: 100 g of C18H32O2 (M = 280.45) reacts with 2*(253.8) g = 507.6/2.8045 ~ 181.0 g of iodine, exactly the number quoted on page 3.
assumptions: Standard neutral valences C:4, H:1, O:2, P:5 (phosphate P(V) as drawn in fragment b) and the handshake lemma: every sigma/pi bond contributes exactly two valence ends (trusted_general_law).

Reductive ozonolysis cleaves every C=C of an acyclic chain to carbonyls, giving u+1 fragments for u double bonds; 'three different organic products in equimolar amounts' implies u+1 = 3 (trusted_general_law applied to the problem statement).

The 5.1 value n = 1: parity (proved, n_odd) gives n odd; the chirality clause of the problem text (PL1 chiral, all other diastereomers achiral with a plane of symmetry) singles out n = 1, the single H capping the central oxygen of the bridging glycerol (problem_text, re-derived argument documented in answer.md and the lean module docstring).

The page-4 hydrolysis equation (PL1 + 8H2O -> 4RCOOH + 2H3PO4 + 3 glycerol) is a problem statement used as a consistency check; the assembly inventory and the hydrolysis inventory are proved to agree (hydrolysis_consistency, inventory_bridge).
